reviewer.name: Claude Sonnet, fresh subagent (cold reader 1)
reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: DRAFT, three sentences: ‘There are a lot of ways to influence people without engaging their conscious mind. Marketers and interface designers know this perfectly well. The Federal Trade Commission has a report on “dark patterns” - designs that trick or manipulate consumers.’ It appears once in CONTEXT.txt, as the opening three sentences of the second paragraph of ‘Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists’, immediately followed by his unchanged OECD sentence. THE CHANGE: sentence 2 is word for word the source’s second sentence (his, stays); sentences 1 and 3 are the new ones; sentence 3 carries his own ‘designs that trick or manipulate consumers’ and none of the ‘used to’ / ‘trick and manipulate’ wording the_change says failed preservation; the only ‘their’ left is ‘their conscious mind’ in sentence 1, which points to ‘people’ and changes no meaning. So it does what the_change says. MEANING against SOURCE.txt: (1) many ways to influence people that do not go through the conscious mind - kept (source: ‘there are many ways to influence people’ / ‘not actively engaging the conscious mind’; his guide: ‘Influence doesn’t wait for the conscious mind to sign a form’; losing ‘actively’ changes nothing here); (2) marketers and interface designers know it - unchanged; (3) the FTC’s report on dark patterns concerns designs that trick or manipulate consumers - kept (the dash gloss defines the term the way the source’s ‘describe designs that…’ does). No new claim or fact: no year, title, figure or quote added, nothing said about what the report found beyond the source, so C04 is absent. The OECD sentence after it is untouched. READ IN CONTEXT: the paragraph before ends a long list of channels hypnotism can work through; sentence 1 generalises that into influence without the conscious mind (a mild echo of the list, the same step the source’s own opening took); ‘this’ in sentence 2 points back to that claim, ‘their’ points to ‘people’, and the FTC sentence follows from ‘interface designers’ and hands over to the OECD sentence. ‘has a report on’ is casual but natural for his voice; the spaced hyphen is a real appositive gloss for a term many readers will not know (the next paragraph in the section also uses a spaced hyphen, so it is not out of place). TELLS: I walked T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the draft in this context and find none PRESENT. Closest calls: T09/T13 (the D9 prompt) - the paragraph is a claim followed by support in the source’s order, but it keeps his dry aside (‘know this perfectly well’) and the change swaps wording only, so it makes no new equal-weight slots; T26 - ‘influence … without … conscious’ is echoed by the question in the next paragraph, and ‘manipulate’ sits in both the FTC and OECD sentences, but both repeats are in his published guide and do a job (the question sharpens engagement into agreement; the two bodies describe the same thing); T25 - the dash is an appositive, not a colon reveal; T11/T19 - sentence 1 states the claim the following sentences rest on, it does not merely bridge or announce; no first person (T01, C03); nothing reordered or moved (T14); no negative reveal, aphorism, closer or recap (T16, T17, T20, T29); T15 - plain words, and the structure changed, not just the vocabulary. LINTER: ‘D9 follows the source order’ - accepted: only the wording inside the three sentences was swapped, nothing reordered or moved, and T13 and T09 were checked above. E186 ‘without ...ing’ on ‘without engaging their conscious mind’ - accepted: that phrase is the sentence’s whole claim and the source and his guide carry the same negation; what happens instead is answered by the context (the list of channels before it, and steer / deceive / coerce / manipulate after it), and cutting it would remove the premise the rest of the paragraph and the next paragraph’s question rest on. I read the writer’s ADMISSION.json after my own pass; its reasons agree with mine.
